title: Brown bullhead catfish melanoma represents a novel transmissible cancer.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Opened the supplementary workbook (MOESM3, 1 MB, 11 sheets). Supplementary Table 2 lists 93 Lake Memphremagog fish: 51 'Presence of melanistic neoplasia', 42 'Normal'; only 10 fish have a sequenced skin lesion, most samples are healthy brain. Other sheets are summary statistics (read counts, coverage, mean VAF (variant allele frequency) per sample, pairwise copy-number correlations, virus presence, 20-row DESeq2 table). NCBI SRA search on the two BioProjects returned 179 records (17 + 162), all raw sequencing.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That 144,177 tumour-shared SNVs (single-nucleotide variants) exist and that tumours are clonally related; no processed variant table or genotype matrix was found in the supplement, so this rests on the paper. The GitHub scripts repository was not opened.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked: SRA BioProjects PRJNA1284812/PRJNA1284832 are public (179 records) and the supplement downloads; no access application needed.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked: tumour vs normal 'Condition' is a column in Supplementary Table 2, but it is a per-fish clinical label, not a per-row measurement attached to any feature table.

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked: no processed features (variant calls, expression matrix) are deposited; inputs would have to be rebuilt from raw whole-genome short and long reads, which project rules forbid downloading.

a4_units_stated.note: Checked: supplementary summary tables state units (coverage X, Mb, VAF fraction); not relevant given no feature table.

a5_enough_rows.note: Checked: 93 fish in Supplementary Table 2, only ~10 with sequenced tumour–normal pairs (17 pairs per paper text); far below 400 for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Hundreds of GB to TB of raw reads (e.g. ~500M read pairs per reference sample, 25–87 Gb per long-read sample, seen in Supp Tables 4–5)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Checked: per-sample raw data volumes in the supplement imply a working set far above 5 GB; variant calling needs a cluster.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Checked: 93 sample rows and 179 SRA records are consistent with the paper's description of a sampled subset plus reference fish and RNA-seq.

a8_label_provenance.note: Tumour status is a visual/histological field observation, not a model output.

honest_claim_h3: With ~10 tumour–normal pairs from one lake, a model could at best claim to distinguish this one clonal tumour lineage from host tissue, which the paper already shows with simple variant sharing.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use genome-wide genetic variants from catfish tissue to classify samples as transmissible tumour versus host tissue.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-sample variant profiles rebuilt from raw whole-genome reads; about 93 fish listed, only about 10 with sequenced tumours (verified in Supplementary Table 2).
plain_idea.predict: Whether a tissue sample is tumour or normal, with the true answer from field and histology observation of melanistic lesions.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Little: tumour versus host is already trivially separable by shared variants, so there is no open prediction problem at this sample size.

ml_idea: None viable: a population-genomics discovery paper with ~93 fish, ~10 tumour–normal pairs, and only raw sequencing deposited.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A because features require cluster-scale variant calling from raw reads.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count tumour samples with sequence data in Supplementary Table 2: about 10, which kills it.

verdict_reason: Fails A3, A5 and A6: only raw whole-genome reads are deposited (no processed variant table), 93 fish with ~10 sequenced tumours is far too few rows, and rebuilding features needs cluster-scale compute. The existing-models search was skipped because the project died at Part A.
